# Spatial Hierarchies
Also called: Spatial Tree Structures
## Overview
Spatial Hierarchies organize data into [tree structures](#4139-tree-based-structures-octree-pointer-tree-sparse-voxel-dag.md) to accelerate point location via recursive search [S1, unofficial]. They solve the problem of inefficient traversal in sparse scenes by reducing intersection tests [G]. Unlike sibling methods such as [Hierarchical Spatial Enumeration Optimization](1663-hierarchical-spatial-enumeration-optimization.md) or [Jiang et al. Acceleration Structure](1673-jiang-et-al-acceleration-structure.md), they dynamically partition space rather than relying on fixed grids or image-order traversal.
## Shared principles
For the shared family principles, see [Hierarchical Data Structures](15869-hierarchical-data-structures.md) [G].
## Subtopics

### [Insertion into Spatial Hierarchies](13180-insertion-into-spatial-hierarchies.md)
[Insertion into spatial hierarchies](#13180-insertion-into-spatial-hierarchies.md) refers to the algorithmic process of adding primitives into an existing or growing hierarchical data structure. Unlike static build methods that analyze the entire scene at once, insertion methods process primitives one by one, allowing for incremental updates. This makes it suitable for dynamic environments, though it is highly sensitive to the order of insertion. It is chosen when scenes require frequent updates or when building from unsorted data [G].

## Background
Spatial hierarchies such as octtrees, BSP trees, and KD trees were developed to optimize point location by recursive search [S1, unofficial].
